subject: Boundary cases: incident logs, backups, and our 'no training' promise
messages:
From: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@fastpay.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: security@fastpay.com

Subject: Boundary cases: incident logs, backups, and our 'no training' promise

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the demo last week — all useful context. Our InfoSec team had a couple of follow-ups after reviewing the security questionnaire you sent: they want explicit clarification on a few edge cases tied to your "we do not train on customer data" assurance. Can you confirm behavior for the following?

1) Incident logs: when a customer reports a production anomaly and sends log snippets (stack traces, request IDs) to support, are those logs ever used in model training or tuning? If not, where and how long are they retained?

2) Backups and snapshots: do any automatic storage snapshots or long-term backups ever get processed by model pipelines (even indirectly, e.g., through analytics jobs)?

3) Cache/KV store contents: we understand KV caches are ephemeral, but what is the max TTL and are there any circumstances where cache entries are persisted to longer-term storage?

4) Internal debugging copies: when an engineer pulls customer data to reproduce an issue in a non-prod environment, what controls ensure that copy cannot be consumed by training jobs or experiment pipelines?

Attached: our trimmed security questionnaire and an anonymized sample of the log we looked at.

Appreciate a short, point-by-point response we can include in our internal review.

Best,
Alex
Alex Taylor
Security Engineering
FastPay

Subject: Re: Boundary cases: incident logs, backups, and our 'no training' promise

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear list. I wanted to respond quickly and loop in Vanessa (platform ops) and Marissa (privacy/compliance) who run the retention and dev-access policies. Below are concise answers; I'll follow up with references to internal runbooks and a Drive link.

1) Incident logs: We do not use customer incident logs for model training. Log snippets submitted to support are ingested into our ticketing system and retained according to our Support Data Retention policy (default 90 days searchable, 365 days archived metadata only). The ticket data is tagged as "no-train" in our ingestion pipeline so it is excluded from any training or eval data pools.

2) Backups and snapshots: Automatic storage snapshots are managed by cluster storage and are treated as infrastructure artifacts. They are never piped into model training or analytics model pipelines. Retention for snapshots depends on the environment: hosted production snapshots are kept for 30 days by default; long-term backups (customer-requested exports) are kept per contract. We never stage backups into training buckets.

3) Cache/KV stores: Short-lived KV caches used for inference have a TTL of 24 hours by default and are purged by the runtime. In exceptional cases where we persist a cache for debugging, it is written to an encrypted diagnostics store with a strict 7-day TTL and labeled "diagnostics-no-train"—those stores are excluded from our training ingestion.

4) Internal debugging copies: Engineers must request access via our support incident workflow. Any extracted customer data for reproduction must be stored in an isolated debug sandbox with access controls and an automated deletion hook (default 14 days). Access requires approval and the sandbox is segregated from training/data science clusters; we enforce ACLs and audit logs to prevent accidental use in experiments.

I'll paste the internal runbook links in a follow-up message and attach the relevant excerpt. Let me know if you need explicit contract language or a signed attestation for procurement.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Hi Alex — adding a few operational specifics so you have granular language for your review:

• Snapshots/backups: Production EBS-style snapshots are retained 30 days by default; we also retain compacted metadata (checksum, timestamp, resource id) for 13 months for billing and audit purposes. Neither the snapshot objects nor the compacted metadata are included in training data.

• Analytics/ETL jobs: We run strictly-scoped ETL pipelines; any job that touches customer content is required to carry a data-classification header. Pipelines marked with "for-training" require explicit approvals and are impossible to run against datasets tagged "customer_production" without a documented exception and signoff.

• Debugging copies: When engineers repro an issue using customer-provided content, we require they use the 'diagnostic sandbox' which has network egress disabled and a mandatory deletion cron. We also require an entry in the Debug Access Log (link below) so your team can audit who pulled data and why.

Links:
- Internal retention runbook (view only): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B_example_internal_policy
- Debug Access Log (read-only): HS-98765

Attachments: excerpt from the retention runbook (pdf).
